simple.meaning: עֲרַב (ʻărab) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to commingle.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 4 times in Daniel, beginning at Daniel 2:41. The surrounding contexts include kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עֲרַב (H6151) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: עֲרַב (ʻărab) / H6151 is traced through Daniel 2:41, Daniel 2:43 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Whereas you saw the feet and toes, part of potters’ clay, and part of iron, it will be a divided kingdom; but there will be in it of the strength of the iron, because you saw the iron mixed with miry clay.

timeline.evidenceText: Whereas you saw the feet and toes, part of potters’ clay, and part of iron, it will be a divided kingdom; but there will be in it of the strength of the iron, because you saw the iron mixed with miry clay.
Whereas you saw the iron mixed with miry clay, they will mingle themselves with the seed of men; but they won’t cling to one another, even as iron does not mix with clay.
